title: Bag of Tricks for Efficient Text Classification
summary: This paper proposes fastText, a simple and efficient linear baseline for text classification that represents sentences as bags of word and n-gram embeddings averaged into a hidden layer with a rank constraint. It uses a hierarchical softmax based on Huffman coding for scalability to large output spaces and the hashing trick for memory-efficient n-gram features. Experiments show fastText achieves accuracy competitive with deep learning classifiers while training orders of magnitude faster, reaching 92.5% test accuracy on AG News with bigrams.

match_target.why: The user explicitly hinted at Table 1, AG News test accuracy, fastText h=10 with bigrams. This is the central sentiment-analysis result and the cheapest to reproduce (1s per epoch on CPU).

tolerance.why: Rule 2: accuracy-like % metric on a test set of 2,000+ examples (AG News test set has 7,600 examples per Zhang et al. 2015); paper prints as percentage so 1.0 absolute.

requirements.stmt: Use a linear model with rank constraint: a look-up table A over words/n-grams whose embeddings are averaged into a text representation, then fed to a linear classifier B.
requirements.quote: The first weight matrix A is a look-up table over the words. The word representations are then averaged into a text representation

requirements.stmt: Use hierarchical softmax based on Huffman coding tree for the output layer.
requirements.quote: we use a hierarchical softmax (Goodman, 2001) based on the Huffman coding tree

requirements.stmt: Use bag of n-grams as additional features to capture local word order.
requirements.quote: we use a bag of n-grams as additional features to capture some partial information about the local word order

requirements.stmt: Use 10 hidden units for the sentiment analysis experiments.
requirements.quote: We use 10 hidden units and run fastText for 5 epochs

requirements.stmt: Select learning rate on a validation set from {0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5}.
requirements.quote: a learning rate selected on a validation set from {0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5}

requirements.stmt: Train with stochastic gradient descent and a linearly decaying learning rate, asynchronously on multiple CPUs.
requirements.quote: This model is trained asynchronously on multiple CPUs using stochastic gradient descent and a linearly decaying learning rate.
